scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling capacity problem: bills are largely correct but CS lacks fast automated response/adjustment tooling, so an AI agent that auto-answers and auto-fixes bills would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill-calculation errors (e.g. in estimate substitution logic), directly causing the dispute surge.

H-AMI-EXPORT-DEGRADATION.statement: The nightly MDMS-to-billing export (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded or began failing around August, causing missing/incorrect AMI reads and forcing estimate substitution that produced wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual meter-read collection or the daily field-to-billing handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded since August, increasing missed/incomplete reads and triggering more estimated bills.

H-DISPUTE-MEASUREMENT-ARTIFACT.statement: The doubling in ticket count reflects a CRM/process or categorization change (e.g. new ticket intake channel or classification) rather than an actual increase in incorrect bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route-completion for manual-read accounts was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep 2026 (9200 manual-read accounts), i.e. a 7-point shortfall in routes completed during the exact dispute-surge window.

CRM response-time stats for 2440 dispute tickets show median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA — response speed is not currently breaching target. This weakens the framing that CS is a handling-capacity/speed bottleneck; it does not speak to whether underlying bills are wrong.

CRM monthly dispute counts rose from 610/590 in June/July 2026 to 1180/1260 in August/September 2026, confirming the roughly two-fold magnitude and the August-onset timing described in the initial request. This establishes the surge's size and window but does not by itself indicate which upstream cause (AMI export, field reads, billing rules, or a measurement artifact) produced it.

billing-db's tariff change log shows zero records, meaning no tariff/rate changes were logged. This rules out a tariff-rate change as the cause of wrong bills, but says nothing about import validation rule logic, AMI reads, field reads, or ticket-handling capacity.

Of 3025 disputed bills, 1785 (59%) had ACTUAL reads and 1240 (41%) had ESTIMATED reads, so a majority of disputed bills are on bills billed from actual meter reads, not estimate-substitution. This weakens any explanation of the dispute surge that relies purely on missing/estimated reads (AMI export or field-read degradation) and points toward a cause that also corrupts actual-read billing, such as a billing import/validation defect.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there has been no tariff change this year; this is a stakeholder claim, not independent evidence, and it agrees with the already-recorded authoritative E-04 finding (zero tariff-change log entries) without adding new information.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a staffing shortfall of three readers since July causes late routes, so affected customers receive estimated bills; this is an unverified stakeholder claim, not independent evidence, from a stakeholder whose incentive is a contract headcount increase. It temporally aligns with the Aug-Sep route-completion shortfall (E-01) but, per E-05, estimated reads are a minority (41%) of disputed bills, so even if true it explains only part of the surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (§4.2) confirms the utility may request field route priority changes, but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) — this is the documentary basis for the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update, not new causal information about the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) identifies 14 individual manual-read routes with distinct, non-uniform completion rates; the sample shows route R-00 completing only 70% of scheduled reads. This adds route-level granularity beneath the aggregate 0.88 completion rate (E-01), showing the shortfall is concentrated in specific routes rather than spread evenly, but it does not by itself say whether this residual field-read gap matters once the billing-rule root cause (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) is addressed.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) lists 320 accounts billed on estimated reads last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes (sample AC-20000 on route R-00). The returned fields are limited to account_id and route, so this query does not supply the read-type/tariff/import-status detail that W-WI-ANALYZE-DISPUTES intended to use to analyze disputed bills by cause.

U-AMI-EXPORT-STATUS-UNKNOWN.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned mdms-export access (currently ACCESS_PENDING/DEGRADED, no fallback) and review AMI read-event records and H-MDMS-BILL delivery completeness/semantic validity against disputed ACTUAL-read bills.
U-AMI-EXPORT-STATUS-UNKNOWN.safe_placeholder: Proceed with request_mdms_export_access as a pending diagnostic step only; do not attribute causation to the AMI export until access is granted and reviewed.

U-DISPUTE-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY.question: Could part of the ticket-count doubling (E-03) reflect a CRM categorization/intake change rather than a real increase in incorrect bills?
U-DISPUTE-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If part of the surge is a measurement artifact, the dispute-volume-recovery target and the magnitude of billing-import fix needed would be overstated.
U-DISPUTE-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Review crm-tickets intake/categorization configuration history for Aug 2026 for channel or taxonomy changes coincident with the surge.
U-DISPUTE-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat the dispute-volume-recovery target as provisional; keep the raw monthly count (M-DISPUTE-VOLUME) as the tracked metric pending this check.

U-FIELD-ROUTE-REMEDIATION-NEED.question: Once the billing-rule root cause is addressed, does the residual estimated-read dispute share still require a push_route_update to fix the field route completion shortfall (E-01)?

U-FIELD-ROUTE-REMEDIATION-NEED.safe_placeholder: Hold push_route_update pending post-fix remeasurement; do not execute until residual need is confirmed.

U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Does the daily manual-read upload handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) deliver complete and semantically valid reads to billing, or does a delivery/semantic defect in this handoff contribute to the Aug-Sep route-completion shortfall (E-01) and resulting estimated-read disputes?
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If H-FIELD-BILL is itself defective, remediation may need a handoff/process fix in addition to, or instead of, a route-dispatch change, affecting whether push_route_update is the correct remedy.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Review field-dispatch delivery logs and billing-db ingestion timestamps for H-FIELD-BILL during Aug-Sep 2026 to confirm delivery completeness and payload validity.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat push_route_update as pending confirmation of handoff validity; limit scope meanwhile to assess_field_route_impact diagnostics.

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (E-03) because a change to the billing import validation rules around that time is the best-supported locus of systematic bill-calculation errors, consistent with tariff changes being ruled out (E-04) and with the majority (59%, 1785/3025) of disputed bills being billed from ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimates (E-05), i.e. the defect affects both read paths, not just estimate substitution. payload.summary: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (E-03) because a change to the billing import validation rules around that time is the best-supported locus of systematic bill-calculation errors, consistent with tariff changes being ruled out (E-04) and with the majority (59%, 1785/3025) of disputed bills being billed from ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimates (E-05), i.e. the defect affects both read paths, not just estimate substitution. This is a bill-correctness problem in the billing-import step, not a ticket-handling capacity shortfall, since dispute response times remain inside the 3.0-day SLA (E-02).
